reference_audit.finding: Existing Julia reference has genuine loss kernels but converts all inputs to Float32 before target products and exponentials, unlike native Float16-rounded products and Float64 exponentials. Corrected storage-type product and narrowing sequence; this is a precision/mapping fidelity correction, not a proven wrong-output historical failure.

algorithm: Per-position masked weighted loss backward across81 classes, with native Float32 sum/exponential-product intermediates and precision-specific storage
mapping: One64-thread-grid workitem per spatial position, sequential81-class loop; one selected batch

native_to_julia_mapping.reason: Preserves native mixed-precision narrowing; Float32 and Half exponential implementations differ, checked at original tolerance

keyconfounds: Float64 storage retains Float32 intermediate narrowing by native design

scientific_intent.scientific_task: Compute gradient-like outputs over class channels and spatial positions
scientific_intent.governing_method: Native masked weighted log-softmax backward formula
scientific_intent.discretization: 81 classes by8732 positions, one selected batch
scientific_intent.input_regime: negative dyadic log inputs and positive weights; both masks and all target classes
scientific_intent.precision_sensitivity: Half-rounded target products and exponentials; Float64 exponentials narrowed into Float32 intermediates
scientific_intent.community_use_case: Dense classification or detection loss primitive; no training convergence claims

observation: The benchmark uses a mixed-precision loss formula even for Float64 storage. The study preserves those narrowing points and checks every output in one complete original-size batch slice. Agreement establishes this kernel contract; it does not establish a canonical cross-entropy gradient or training behavior.
